newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Strikers stop Latin America's biggest port.
newsitem.headline: Strikers stop Latin America's biggest port.

text.p: Workers at the Brazilian port of Santos, the largest in Latin America, began a fresh strike on Tuesday and threatened it could spread to the national level by Wednesday.

Workers massed in front of the terminal of steel company Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) at Santos to protest against the company's recent policy of using its own workers to load and unload vessels rather than employing union members.
The crowd, estimated at between 500 and 2,000 people, built barricades on the road leading to the terminal and set tires on fire, an official at Cosipa said.
"The situation is very tense here," he added.
Port officials said it was possible the crowd would swell to several thousand as more people were being brought in by bus.
Military police officers in the early hours evacuated 26 stevedores who had occupied two vessels at the Cosipa terminal for the last 13 days.
No one was reported injured in the operation or during the demonstrations, a port spokeswoman said. But tension was rising. "People are really upset, some are crying," she said.
Delegates from other ports were scheduled to meet in the afternoon to decide whether the strike should spread to the national level. If so, it would be the second national port strike in two weeks.

Labour unrest has risen sharply since the implementation of a new Brazilian port modernisation law. Unions say they favour increasing competitivity between ports but this should not lead to cuts in the labour force.
